newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladeshis scramble out of Dhaka for festival.
newsitem.headline: Bangladeshis scramble out of Dhaka for festival.

text.p: Tens of thousands of Bangladeshis crammed into buses, trains and ferries on Friday as they left the capital Dhaka to celebrate the Moslem Eid al-Fitr festival with friends and relatives in the countryside.
While the bustling capital of nine million people has enjoyed a welcome ease in traffic jams since the week-long Eid holiday started on Thursday, congestion elsewhere has worsened.
Witnesess said hundreds of vehicles were backed up on either side of the Jamuna river north of Dhaka.
Jamuna is the gateway to northern Bangladesh but crossing it by ferry has become difficult because the water level has dropped sharply over the past few years.
Thousands of people clambored on to the roofs of packed buses and trains while river ferries sailed off stacked with passengers in defiance of warnings by navigation authorities.
Dhaka officials said about two million residents left the city on Thursday and a similar number would follow on Friday.
Eid al-Fitr, Islam's biggest festival marking the end of the fasting month of Ramadan, is due to be celebrated on Sunday or Monday depending on the sighting of the new moon.
